sanity_expectations: Exact zeros occur when s=0 or i=0 by formula, though the sampled ranges mostly stay away from those boundaries.
For fixed c,s,i, new_infection_rate increases linearly with c because c is a pure multiplicative prefactor.
At fixed c and moderate i, sweeping q from low to high should move the rate from near zero toward an order-s*c bounded regime, not an unbounded power law.

Comparing two s strata at fixed c while varying q*i through the transition region, the normalized rate new_infection_rate/(s*c) should show visibly different curvature because both the effective threshold and the exponent depend on s.

Comparing conditions with similar q*i and the same s but different i, responses should generally fail to collapse to one curve because i enters not only through q*i but also through infectious_threshold_modulation, infectious_curvature_modulation, and the redundancy factor.

With infectious_redundancy_shape=1.5>0, increasing i at fixed q,s,c should amplify the rate beyond the single-Hill parent more strongly when q*i is not too large; this extra factor weakens toward 1 as q*i becomes large because of the denominator 1+q*i.
All sampled outputs should remain finite and real over the specified domain with the chosen parameter values.

rationale: Structure check shows no derivatives, no integrals, and an explicit algebraic solution for new_infection_rate, so this is an explicit static mapping rather than any ODE. Per the freedom decision, preserve declared sampled inputs c, i, s, q as independent variables and keep the named modulation symbols fixed as parameters. Ranges are chosen to expose the intended mechanisms without collapsing into trivial limits: s and i stay mostly within biologically admissible fractions away from the exact zero boundary, while still allowing low and high prevalence/susceptibility strata; q spans low to high infectious opportunity so the effective exposure q*i ranges from about 5e-4 to 2.7, which crosses well below and well above the chosen half-saturation scale 0.15 after threshold modulation. This ensures visible transition from near-zero response to the bounded contact-limited regime instead of placing all samples deep in saturation or entirely linear. c is varied as an external contact-rate condition because the static freedom decision keeps it as a sampled axis; its range changes the contact-limited ceiling s*c but does not remove the nonlinear contrasts. Parameter values are set away from parent-recovery limits: susceptible_saturation_modulation=3 makes the effective threshold vary appreciably with s; susceptible_curvature_modulation=1.2 and infectious_curvature_modulation=1.0 make the exposure-response shape differ across susceptible and infectious strata while keeping the exponent 1 + 1.2*s + 1.0*i positive over the chosen domain (>1.07); infectious_threshold_modulation=2 creates a clear i-dependent threshold shift while preserving 1+infectious_threshold_modulation*i>0; infectious_redundancy_shape=1.5 activates the added bounded prevalence-dependent shape factor without violating positivity, since 1 + infectious_redundancy_shape*i/(1+q*i) remains >1 on the chosen domain. These conditions explicitly address the distinguishing comparisons in the mechanism notes: at fixed c, varying q*i across the transition region and comparing different s values reveals normalized curvature changes; matching or comparing nearby q*i values across different i values does not collapse the response because i also shifts threshold, curvature, and the redundancy factor. Weak effect note: very small i and q together still produce near-zero rates, so mechanistic contrasts are weakest there, but the broader sampled domain includes the informative mid-range transition regime.

scenario_text: Estimate the instantaneous rate at which susceptible people acquire infection under independently sampled contact and infectiousness conditions. The baseline mechanism is infectious contact generation with a contact-limited acquisition response that approaches a finite ceiling at high exposure. Susceptibility and infectious prevalence are treated as externally specified conditions rather than evolving states. The output is an instantaneous epidemiological rate, so no time integration is required.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed s and c, new_infection_rate increases with exposure q*i as a one-parameter Michaelis-Menten saturating curve with a single shared half-saturation scale exposure_half_saturation independent of susceptible availability.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same bounded contact-limited acquisition mechanism but relax the assumption that the half-saturation scale is fixed: make effective saturation depend on susceptible fraction so that crowding of susceptible encounters changes the curvature of the exposure-response while preserving vanishing at i=0 and s=0 and a finite high-exposure ceiling.
response_change.observable_effect: When q*i is varied at fixed c, the rise toward saturation is steeper or more delayed depending on s; thus two strata with different s show different exposure-response curvature that cannot be matched by one parent half-saturation value.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when susceptible fraction varies meaningfully away from a narrow constant band while q*i spans values below and above exposure_half_saturation; especially informative for intermediate exposure where curvature is identifiable and 0 < s <= 1.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest variation in s already reveals that the exposure-response bends differently at the same q*i; in holdout, broader s variation extends this same curvature difference rather than introducing a new mechanism.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where susceptible dependence of the effective half-saturation vanishes, so the saturation scale becomes the constant exposure_half_saturation for all s.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a single susceptibility-independent exposure half-saturation, so all susceptible strata share the same normalized exposure-response shape after multiplication by s.
plan.baseline_assumption: The effective-exposure level at which acquisition reaches half of its contact-limited maximum is fixed and does not vary with the susceptible fraction.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Encounter competition and repeated contact among the shrinking susceptible pool can change how quickly additional infectious exposure converts into new acquisitions, making the apparent saturation scale depend on susceptible availability.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-threshold assumption already present in the saturating acquisition term, not to add a wholly separate process. The parent mapping is s*c times a saturating function of q*i with one shared half-saturation parameter, so changing s only rescales the curve vertically. Scientifically, if the susceptible pool is sparse or dense, the same infectious exposure can be distributed differently across susceptible encounter opportunities, altering how quickly the acquisition response approaches its contact-limited ceiling. Vary q*i while holding c fixed and compare two admissible susceptible fractions s1 and s2 within 0<s<=1. In the parent, the ratio new_infection_rate/(s*c) as a function of q*i is identical for both strata, because curvature is controlled only by exposure_half_saturation. In the child, that normalized curve changes with s, giving an observable curvature contrast at intermediate exposures. This is a true target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the predicted instantaneous rate for the same supplied inputs changes. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce different normalized q*i-response shapes across varying s; it can only choose one common threshold and one common curvature family. The refinement remains scientifically admissible because the rate stays nonnegative, vanishes when s=0 or i=0, and can be constructed to retain a finite high-exposure bound.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when q and s are held approximately fixed and i varies over a non-negligible admissible range away from zero, especially in moderate exposure regimes where the response is neither near zero nor already fully saturated.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, varying q*i at fixed s may suggest one common threshold; in holdout with matched q*i achieved through different i values, the refined law shows distinct response levels because infectious prevalence changes the effective threshold surface, not just total exposure.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when infectious-prevalence modulation of the threshold is absent, so the half-saturation depends only on s.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes that once q*i is formed, infectious prevalence i has no further role in shaping the location of the acquisition threshold; different mixtures of many weakly infectious sources versus fewer stronger opportunities are treated as equivalent whenever q*i matches.
plan.baseline_assumption: Equivalent effective exposures with the same product q*i produce the same fractional acquisition response at fixed s, implying a single threshold surface determined only by susceptible availability.
plan.scientific_mechanism: At equal q*i, distributing exposure across a larger infectious fraction can change overlap, independence, or redundancy of infectious contacts, shifting the apparent exposure level needed to reach half of the contact-limited acquisition maximum.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's strict q*i collapse. The parent already includes susceptible-dependent curvature and saturation, but it still imposes a single threshold in the exposure coordinate q*i for each s. Scientifically, independently sampled contact and infectiousness conditions need not make prevalence composition irrelevant: with fixed susceptible fraction s and fixed per-contact opportunity q, changing i can alter whether exposure is spread across many infectious contacts or concentrated into fewer opportunities, which changes redundancy and therefore the apparent threshold for acquisition. The concrete distinguishing condition is: hold s and q fixed, compare two admissible i levels in a moderate regime where q*i is large enough to generate measurable infection but not so large that the response is fully saturated. The parent predicts that the response depends only on q*i, so data collapsed by q*i must coincide under one shared parameter set. The child predicts a shifted threshold across i levels even after matching or comparing nearby q*i values. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because new_infection_rate itself changes as a function of supplied inputs. No new degree of freedom is needed conceptually because the refinement can be implemented by making the existing threshold structure depend on i using additional fixed parameters in the successor equation. Limitation: if all observed conditions remain extremely close to i=0 or deep in saturation, the contrast will be weak.

Vary i across an admissible range and q so that q*i sweeps from below to above the transition region, while holding s fixed at an intermediate positive value. In the parent, once the threshold shift from infectious_threshold_modulation is accounted for, all q*i response curves at that s have the same steepness because the exponent is fixed by s alone. In the child, increasing i can also change steepness, producing a broader or sharper transition at equal s and similar threshold location. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the observable relation from supplied inputs (s,i,q,c) to new_infection_rate changes directly. The effect is scientifically admissible under the same static observation protocol, remains nonnegative and bounded by the contact-limited ceiling, and disappears continuously when the added i-dependent curvature contribution is set to zero. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot generally match two different i-conditioned curve shapes at the same s because it has only one curvature value per s.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed s, the rate is a single Hill-like saturating function of exposure q*i with one shared curvature exponent 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s and one effective half-saturation scale modified by s and i.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same bounded contact-limited structure but relax the assumption that infectious prevalence only shifts the threshold; allow infectious prevalence to also alter the steepness/cooperativity of the exposure-acquisition response, so the q*i to rate curve changes shape with i as well as location.
response_change.observable_effect: For two admissible infectious prevalences with the same susceptible fraction held fixed, the low-exposure rise and mid-exposure sharpness can differ even after matching the half-saturation location; the parent can slide the curve horizontally with i but cannot reproduce an i-dependent steepness change with one shared parameter set.

contract.activation_condition: Visible when q*i traverses the transition region around the effective half-saturation and i varies over a non-negligible admissible range while s is held fixed away from zero; weak at very low exposure, near-complete saturation, or i so small that prevalence-dependent steepness changes are negligible.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate variation in i already reveals that equalized threshold location does not align the full response curves; in holdout, extending to higher i amplifies the same mechanism through stronger prevalence-dependent steepness differences without changing the bounded high-exposure ceiling.
contract.continuation_path: Setting the added infectious-prevalence curvature effect to zero recovers the parent law exactly.
contract.scientific_mechanism: As infectious people become more prevalent, contacts may become more redundant or more independently distributed across susceptible individuals, changing how sharply additional exposure converts into acquisition even at the same aggregate q*i.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the exponent governing the saturating transition is now input-dependent in i, changing the family of admissible curve shapes rather than merely rescaling or shifting one shared shape.
contract.assumption_before: Infectious prevalence affects the target mapping only through q*i and the threshold factor (1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i), leaving the Hill-like curvature fixed at a given s.
contract.assumption_after: Infectious prevalence also modulates the curvature exponent of the bounded acquisition response, so i changes transition sharpness as well as threshold.
contract.after_fragment: s*c*(q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i)/(exposure_half_saturation/((1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s)*(1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i)) + (q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i))
contract.observable_signature: Hold s fixed at an intermediate positive value and vary q so that q*i spans the transition region for two different admissible i values. In the parent, after accounting for the i-dependent threshold shift, both curves share the same steepness because the exponent is fixed at 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s. In the child, the same comparison shows different low-exposure rise and mid-transition sharpness because the exponent also changes with i. This is directly observable in the scored mapping from supplied inputs (s,i,q,c) to new_infection_rate and is strongest away from near-zero exposure and away from full saturation.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent cannot generally match two i-conditioned response curves with different steepness at the same fixed s because it has only one curvature value 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s for that s. Retuning exposure_half_saturation or infectious_threshold_modulation only shifts the curve location with i; it does not create prevalence-dependent sharpening or broadening once threshold location is matched.

range_suggestions.infectious_curvature_modulation: [-1, 10] with 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i > 0 over the admissible (s,i) range

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed s, the acquisition probability per susceptible is a single Hill-type saturating function of aggregate exposure q*i, with one shared effective threshold and one shared curvature value determined only by linear modulation in s and i.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed s, the exposure-acquisition relation transitions from near-linear response at low infectious prevalence to stronger saturation at higher infectious prevalence because infectious prevalence not only shifts threshold/curvature but also changes how close contact opportunities are to independent across susceptibles, producing a prevalence-dependent saturation shape that cannot be represented by one single-phase Hill form over all i.
response_change.observable_effect: When q and s are held fixed and i is varied from low to moderate values, the child can show a delayed onset of strong saturation at low i but a sharper approach to the contact ceiling at higher i; the parent can only bend this tradeoff through one Hill family and cannot match both low-i near-proportional growth and high-i compressed approach-to-ceiling with one shared parameter set.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, variation in i at fixed s and q can reveal mild deviation from a single Hill phase; in holdout, the same mechanism becomes clearer when q*i extends further into the saturating regime, exposing different low-i versus high-i approach shapes to the same contact ceiling.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added prevalence-dependent shape refinement is set to zero so the exposure-response remains a single Hill-type saturating function with the existing threshold and curvature modulation.
plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes one single-phase Hill-type acquisition response to aggregate exposure, so infectious prevalence can only alter threshold and exponent smoothly within that same family.
plan.baseline_assumption: All infectious-contact opportunities are effectively summarized by one homogeneous saturating exposure-response phase, with no additional prevalence-dependent transition between near-independent and redundant contact opportunity sampling.
plan.scientific_mechanism: As infectious prevalence rises, contacts experienced by susceptibles can shift from approximately independent rare opportunities to more redundant repeated opportunities from overlapping infectious sources, changing the shape of saturation itself rather than only the threshold or Hill exponent.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase exposure-response assumption. The parent already lets s and i modulate the threshold and curvature, but it still forces all observations onto one Hill-type saturating family. Vary i while holding s and q fixed, over admissible 0<=i<=1 with q*i crossing the effective half-saturation region. Under the child mechanism, low i corresponds to more nearly independent infectious opportunities and therefore a more gradual early rise, whereas higher i creates more redundant overlap and a more compressed final approach to the same finite contact-limited ceiling. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the instantaneous new_infection_rate versus supplied inputs changes directly. A single refit of the parent parameters may mimic part of this behavior locally, but cannot generally match both the low-i and higher-i shape regimes simultaneously when both are present in the sampled domain. The effect is scientifically limited if data stay entirely in the unsaturated low-exposure regime or if i remains extremely small, where both parent and child collapse toward approximately linear dependence on q*i.

baseline_mechanisms: Infectious contacts create opportunities for transmission.
Acquisition is limited by finite contact opportunities and susceptible availability.
baseline_assumptions: Population composition is fixed during the instantaneous observation.
All individuals represented by the sampled fractions have comparable contact opportunities.
The sampled infectiousness level summarizes pathogen and host effects without separate within-host dynamics.
There is no explicit spatial structure or temporal memory.
scientific_constraints: The target rate and all fractions must be nonnegative.
The susceptible and infectious fractions cannot exceed one.
The target must vanish when either the susceptible or infectious fraction is zero.
The high-exposure response is bounded by a finite contact-related maximum.
refinement_agenda: Add heterogeneous contact activity across subpopulations.
Replace the fixed population fractions with evolving epidemiological compartments.
Add spatial or network structure to contact opportunities.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed s and c, new_infection_rate increases with exposure q*i as a one-parameter Michaelis-Menten saturating curve with a single shared half-saturation scale exposure_half_saturation independent of susceptible availability.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same bounded contact-limited acquisition mechanism but relax the assumption that the half-saturation scale is fixed: make effective saturation depend on susceptible fraction so that crowding of susceptible encounters changes the curvature of the exposure-response while preserving vanishing at i=0 and s=0 and a finite high-exposure ceiling.
response_change.observable_effect: When q*i is varied at fixed c, the rise toward saturation is steeper or more delayed depending on s; thus two strata with different s show different exposure-response curvature that cannot be matched by one parent half-saturation value.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when susceptible fraction varies meaningfully away from a narrow constant band while q*i spans values below and above exposure_half_saturation; especially informative for intermediate exposure where curvature is identifiable and 0 < s <= 1.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest variation in s already reveals that the exposure-response bends differently at the same q*i; in holdout, broader s variation extends this same curvature difference rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where susceptible dependence of the effective half-saturation vanishes, so the saturation scale becomes the constant exposure_half_saturation for all s.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: susceptible-dependent saturation scale in bounded infection acquisition
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Encounter competition and repeated contact among the shrinking susceptible pool can change how quickly additional infectious exposure converts into new acquisitions, making the apparent saturation scale depend on susceptible availability.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a distinct susceptibility-controlled relaxation scale inside the nonlinear denominator, changing the shape of the exposure-response family across s rather than merely shifting one global gain or one global threshold.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The effective-exposure level at which acquisition reaches half of its contact-limited maximum is fixed and does not vary with the susceptible fraction.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The effective half-saturation scale is modulated by susceptible availability, so different susceptible fractions have different exposure-response curvature even under the same contact rate and infectious exposure.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Set susceptible_saturation_modulation = 0 to recover the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: For fixed c, compare normalized rate new_infection_rate/(s*c) versus q*i across two admissible susceptible fractions with 0 < s <= 1. The parent predicts the same Michaelis-Menten curve in both strata, while the child predicts different curvature because the effective saturation scale is exposure_half_saturation/(1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s).
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent cannot reproduce this pattern because its normalized mapping new_infection_rate/(s*c) depends only on q*i through one common exposure_half_saturation, so all s strata share the same curve shape. The child creates an s-dependent denominator scale, yielding a family of distinct curvature profiles across s that no single parent parameter set can match simultaneously over conditions where both s and q*i vary.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent uses one susceptible-modulated half-saturation scale, so at fixed s the dependence of new_infection_rate on exposure q*i is a standard single Michaelis-type rise with a fixed shape, and changing s mainly rescales the overall prefactor and shifts that one threshold.
response_change.child_relation: Refine the acquisition response so that susceptible availability also changes the curvature of the exposure-response, not only its half-saturation location, making the q*i to new_infection_rate mapping steeper at low exposure and more abruptly saturating when s is high.
response_change.observable_effect: Across low versus high susceptible fraction, with c fixed and exposure q*i swept through the half-saturation regime, the child shows different normalized response shapes after matching low-exposure slope or half-saturation, whereas the parent can only shift one common saturating curve.

evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that the added susceptible dependence of response shape vanishes, leaving only the original susceptible effect on the half-saturation scale.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: susceptible-dependent curvature of the exposure-limited acquisition response
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Heterogeneity in who remains susceptible can make incremental exposure more cooperative or more concentrated as s changes, altering the curvature of the exposure-to-acquisition response even without adding new state dynamics.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because susceptibility now changes the exponent on the exposure term, altering the balance between the competing half-saturation term and exposure term across the exposure range. evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Acquisition follows a single-shape contact-limited saturation in q*i, with susceptible dependence entering only through a shared threshold parameter.

evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Set susceptible_curvature_modulation = 0 to recover the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At fixed c, compare low and high s while sweeping q*i through the regime around exposure_half_saturation/(1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s): after accounting for the overall s prefactor and threshold shift, the child predicts a sharper, more abruptly saturating normalized response at higher s, unlike the parent's single shared Michaelis shape.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because it only permits one common exposure-response shape with one susceptible-controlled scale. evolution_contracts.before_fragment: s*c*(q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i)/(exposure_half_saturation/((1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s)*(1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i)) + (q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i))
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: s*c*(q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i)/(exposure_half_saturation/((1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s)*(1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i)) + (q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i))*(1 + infectious_redundancy_shape*i/(1 + q*i))
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: The child recovers the parent exactly when infectious_redundancy_shape = 0.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Hold s and q fixed and vary i across a range where q*i moves from below to above the effective half-saturation scale: compared with the parent's single Hill-type family, the child shows an i-dependent reshaping of the rise toward the contact-limited ceiling, weak at very low i and stronger at moderate i where redundancy activates.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot generally absorb this change because the parent only permits i to act through one effective half-saturation factor and one exponent inside a single Hill form. The child introduces a separate bounded prevalence-dependent shape modulation that alters the relation between low-i growth and higher-i approach-to-ceiling at fixed s and q, so fitting the parent to one regime misfits the other when both are sampled.
